title: LinuxCNC and Tormach probe posts write G10 L20 with positions of the active WCS into a different WCS

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

`onProbeResult` in `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps` (PR #2310) writes the found work offset as:

```
G10 L20 P<SetWorkOffset + 1> X[#5420-#<dev>] Y[#5421-#<dev+1>] ...
```

`#5420`-`#5422` hold the current position in the active WCS. `G10 L20 Pn` sets WCS n so that the current position has the given values in WCS n. When `SetWorkOffset` names a WCS that is not the active WCS, the post writes positions of the active WCS into WCS n. The offset in WCS n is then wrong by the difference between the two WCS origins. A later operation in WCS n cuts in the wrong place. The post shows no message.

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` on `main` has the same pattern (`onProbeResult`, the `G10 L20` block with `#5420`).

## Expected

One of these:

- The post makes the target WCS active (or proves it is active) before it reads `#5420`-`#5422`.
- The post refuses by name a `SetWorkOffset` that is not the WCS of the section.

## Evidence

- Review of PR #2310 (non-blocker 3).
- LinuxCNC G-code reference: `G10 L20` ("the current coordinates become the given values") and the parameters `#5420`-`#5428` (current position in the active coordinate system).

## Done means

- `linuxcnc.cps` and `tormach.cps` write a correct offset when `SetWorkOffset` is not the active WCS, or refuse it by name.
- A test pins the case. If possible, the test reads the program back in an interpreter with two WCS origins.
